title: Employer liability: questions to ask about insurance in Moldova
excerpt: For employers in Moldova: distinguish liability from accident and medical benefits, describe occupations and check the proposed conditions.
imageAlt: Employees reviewing a safety checklist in a furniture workshop
author: ING Broker editorial team

seo.title: Employer liability insurance questions in Moldova | ING Broker
seo.description: Prepare occupations, locations and existing benefits for an employer liability discussion. Distinguish legal duties, accident policies and medical services.
seo.keywords: employer liability Moldova, employers insurance, employee accident insurance differences, workforce risk assessment

content:
Assessing employer liability starts with the company's activities and potential employee claims. Do not assume accident insurance or a medical benefit serves the same purpose. Request a written distinction between these products and obligations remaining with the employer.

Describe actual work, not only the business sector

A company may have office employees, drivers and field teams. For assessment, prepare an overview by occupation, workplace and actual activity without names or medical information at the initial stage. Mention work at height, travel and subcontractor participation where relevant. The business sector alone does not explain how these different groups perform their work.

  • Who falls within the persons defined in the proposal?
  • Which claims are considered and under what conditions?
  • How is work away from the office or abroad treated?
  • Which limits, deductibles and notification procedures are proposed?
  • How do existing accident, health and liability policies relate?

Organise a prevention and insurance file

Collect risk assessments, training records and incident history in an internal file. It helps discussion with specialists but does not replace verification of legal occupational-safety obligations. For an actual accident or dispute, seek legal assistance and follow applicable procedures. This article does not establish legal deadlines or liability, and the preparation list should not be used as a safety manual.

Check the file before comparing offers

Compare the activity description with the submitted assessment form. Ensure important occupation groups appear in both. If a workshop sometimes runs two shifts but the form describes office hours only, clarify the difference before comparing premiums. Do not artificially simplify work descriptions to obtain an apparently easier proposal.

Check locations and travel likewise. A team installing goods at customer sites must not be described as office-only. Mark planned activities and ask how to declare them when they begin. Distinguish current operations from intentions, without claiming an existing offer automatically extends to future work.

Explain only the actual benefit to employees

After choosing a policy or benefit, communicate only what documents confirm. Avoid statements that every medical problem or accident is covered. Identify the internal contact who explains procedures and provide access to relevant information. Update communications when products change at renewal. Old presentations must not promise conditions absent from the current contract. Use agreed channels, not public messaging groups, for personal or medical information.

Headcount alone does not describe the risk

Two companies with the same headcount can perform very different activities. Staff in one may work at computers. In another, some employees deliver goods, work in a workshop or attend customer premises. Group people by actual activity and workplace when preparing assessment. Do not initially send names, diagnoses or copies of personal documents where aggregate information is sufficient.

For each category, record ordinary tasks, travel and seasonal changes. Include important occasional duties, not only the title in an organisational chart. An administrative employee who periodically helps with deliveries should be described according to actual work. This information supports assessment but does not establish legal liability in an accident or confirm acceptance of every declared activity.

Liability, accidents and health are different commitments

Accident insurance is considered through its specified events and benefits. A medical benefit concerns services or expenses accepted under its own conditions. Employer liability assessment concerns claims and situations under a distinct contract. An accident benefit payment does not prove the employer is released from every other obligation.

Prepare a list of existing contracts and record each purpose. If a document is only a clinic subscription, name it correctly. If it is a group insurance policy, check the insurer, included persons and specified risks. Before adding a product, identify the need that remains unresolved in the specialists' assessment. More documents do not automatically provide complete protection.

An activity sheet for a workshop and delivery business

In an illustrative company, there are administrators, workshop operators and delivery drivers. Prepare three groups without individual names initially. Describe machinery and operations for the workshop, handling and travel for deliveries, and work locations or visits for office staff. Do not assign one profile merely to simplify the form.

  • Approximate headcount by occupation and workplace.
  • Work at the premises, in the field and abroad.
  • Subcontractors and temporary staff described separately.
  • Planned changes in production.
  • Documented incident history shared through appropriate channels.

The example does not establish inclusion of every category in a specific offer. It prepares questions. Request the definition of people covered by the proposed conditions and the process for staff changes. If a named list is later necessary, clarify required data and confidentiality before sending it.

The role of training and prevention

Keep training, equipment maintenance and operational records. They can help describe risk and history but do not guarantee that an incident cannot occur. Having insurance does not replace assessment of occupational health and safety obligations applicable to the activity in Moldova.

Do not adapt safety procedures from a commercial article. Consult competent specialists and current documents for legal and technical requirements. This material does not list reporting deadlines, sanctions or statutory duties. The preparation checklist serves a different purpose: explaining operations and questions for the proposed contract.

Limits, deductibles and costs remaining with the company

When comparing offers, request the same structure for per-event and aggregate limits where specified. Ask how several people affected by one situation are treated. Check the deductible, meaning the part of a loss borne under the contract. A large limit on the first page does not explain every sublimit and exclusion; read the relevant definitions as well as the headline amount.

Discuss any defence expenses and the procedure for approving them separately. If a situation is ongoing or known, do not assume a new policy takes it over. Provide the chronology through the agreed channel and request an answer for the actual circumstances. Avoid saying employees are covered for everything, even where several policies exist in the company's portfolio.

When a complaint arrives

Register the document, receipt date, attachments and internal handling. Immediate danger or an emergency requires protection and appropriate intervention first. For insurance, follow the contract procedure and seek guidance. Discussing an incident by telephone does not necessarily replace required notification forms.

Separate facts from conclusions about fault or compensation. Do not promise insurer payments or ask an employee to waive rights to simplify the file. Handle medical and legal records confidentially. The broker can explain communication and requested documents but does not decide legal liability or claim payments.

Renewal when hiring or opening a location

Prepare a summary of changes to headcount, occupations, workplaces, machinery and travel. A new location may change the assessment even where the main activity remains the same. Ask for the procedure applicable to amendments and when any policy update becomes effective. Do not assume new circumstances are included merely because the annual premium has been paid.

At the end of renewal discussion, retain the activity inventory accepted for assessment and the final conditions. Check that the offer's information corresponds to the company's actual situation. Mark any unconfirmed point explicitly and identify who will clarify it. Clear records are useful to management and the person later responsible for insurance correspondence. Keep the final conditions with the same dated activity description so a later colleague can identify the actual basis reviewed rather than relying on an older presentation.

A useful opening question

Instead of asking only how much it costs to insure all employees, explain the need: the company's activities, existing benefits and policies, and the types of claims or expenses you want to understand. Request a distinction between voluntary products and legal obligations. Discussion then begins with an actual need and verifiable limits rather than a general protection promise.

Frequently asked questions from employers

Does a medical subscription cover company liability?

Do not infer this from access to medical services. Request an explicit comparison of the subject and purpose of each actual contract before considering one need resolved by another document.

Must every employee be named at the outset?

Start with aggregate headcount and occupation data. Named information should be transmitted only if necessary, through an agreed channel and with confidentiality requirements respected. An initial activity overview need not become a public employee list.

Is a particular policy compulsory for my company?

Whether a policy is compulsory cannot be inferred from the title of an article. That requirement must be checked for the actual activity and jurisdiction separately from assessment of a voluntary insurance solution.

Next step
